accuracy.evidence: Trigger, feeling and response are kept as separate links, matching CASEL's self-awareness competency (identifying emotions and linking feelings to behaviour) and the DfE Relationships Education mental wellbeing outcomes (recognise and talk about emotions; judge whether feelings and behaviour are proportionate). Early warning body signs and acting while arousal is low follow standard school coping guidance; the when-I-notice / I-will goal format is the implementation-intention form from Gollwitzer's research. No claim says feelings should disappear with age.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips at this age: a single upsetting event treated as a pattern (Sam fall-out day, one-off feedback, Mia club item), confusing a feeling with a behaviour (shouting/stamping feedback in MIXUP and challenge), waiting until a feeling is overwhelming before coping (worry line feedback at each later point), believing growing up removes nerves (then-and-now prediction, 'never' feedback), and vague or impossible goals (goal sort messages).

lab_distinct.evidence: Five mechanics built for reflection over time: a ten-day two-week feelings diary where only the recurring trigger days count, a three-link trigger-feeling-response chain builder with a slip message for each of the six wrong link pairs, a draggable plan flag on a rising worry line that redraws a calmer dashed path when the earliest sign is flagged, an age-5 to age-10 pairing board, and a useful/needs-work goal sort. Passed the 30% shingle gate against flagcope, flagstress, flagcause and flagmood.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner first finds that worry keeps following tests (and is told why the fall-out day is not a pattern), then separates what happened from what was felt and what was done, then sees on the line that a plan used at 2 of 10 keeps the peak at 4 while later flags are rejected, then matches how each trigger is handled better at 10, and finally learns what makes a goal usable.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options the lab then settles: 'one fall-out is a pattern' (tapping that day is rejected as a one-off), 'shouting is a feeling' (it is dropped into Response), and 'use the plan when about to explode' (the 10 of 10 flag is rejected and the early flag flattens the line). A fourth asks whether nerves go away with age; the then-and-now pairs show the feeling stays while the response grows.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge questions with twelve distinct m= messages naming the slip: calling a repeat a one-off, treating a pattern as fixed, labelling an action as a feeling or a trigger, waiting or ignoring a body sign, never-feel and vague goals, hiding as the younger response, judging another child's feeling as wrong, or assuming someone is lying.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation reads at FK grade 4.2 (limit 6.5) with short sentences and everyday examples (tests, hunger, losing a game); adult text reads at grade 7.1 (limit 9.5) and names CASEL, the DfE guidance and the IB PYP strand. Canvas prompts are short and every control is one emoji plus a few words.

no_filler.evidence: Passed the filler regex and the 12% duplicate gate. Kid paragraphs each do one job (what a pattern is, the chain, early signs, one-off versus pattern and goals); adult paragraphs cover the standards, the reflection skill, named mistakes and the when-then goal; the family tip is one concrete fridge diary routine.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark and at desktop in dark for all six steps: the diary switches to two columns of five, chain columns and the dealt card fit, worry-line labels are anchored left and right so 'Tummy feels tight' and 'Tears at the door' are not clipped, the then-and-now cards wrap inside their boxes; the canvas grows taller on narrow screens (tall 1.3).

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe WCAG 2.1 AA clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13, every task completed via Show me, no console errors. Every drag or tap has a button route (one button per diary day, Trigger/Feeling/Response buttons, a flag button per time point, age 5 and age 10 card buttons, goal sort buttons); the canvas aria-label reports repeats found, the current card, flag position and worry level, matches and the current goal.
